Markout measured from fill price. At t=0 the value equals EV captured (fill price vs microprice). A declining curve indicates adverse selection eroding edge over time. Red dashed line = breakeven. Buy = bought YES (long); Sell = sold YES (short).

Price bucket chart: fills grouped by the price they were filled at. Shaded bands = 95% CI (naive SE = std/√n). Fills within the same event (e.g. multiple spread brackets on one basketball game) are correlated — their markouts move together. The naive SE (std/√N) treats fills as independent and overstates statistical significance. The cluster-robust SE groups fills by event and accounts for within-event correlation. The design effect (cluster SE / naive SE) shows how much correlation inflates uncertainty; values > 2 mean the effective sample size is < 25% of the raw fill count. If the worst-markout events are concentrated in a few correlated clusters, the session-wide markout may be driven by one or two bad outcomes rather than a systematic edge problem.
